sections.title: Laws on Sexual Morality
observations: This section outlines the prohibitions against various forms of sexual immorality, emphasizing the importance of holiness among God's people.
The chapter begins with a call to the Israelites to be distinct from the practices of the Egyptians and Canaanites, highlighting the need for a unique identity as God's chosen people.
The laws serve not only as moral guidelines but also as a means to maintain the covenant relationship between God and Israel.

sections.title: Consequences of Immorality
observations: The text warns of the severe consequences that come from engaging in the practices listed, including the idea that such actions can lead to the land itself becoming defiled.
This reflects the theological principle that sin has communal and environmental repercussions, not just individual consequences.
The call to holiness is not merely personal but communal, as the actions of individuals can affect the entire community.

importantVerses.commentary: You shall therefore keep my statutes and my rules; if a person does them, he shall live by them: I am the Lord.
So keep my charge never to practice any of these abominable customs that were practiced before you, and never to make yourselves unclean by them: I am the Lord your God.

questions: What does it mean to be holy as God is holy in the context of sexual morality?
How do the prohibitions in Leviticus 18 relate to contemporary discussions on sexuality?
What are the implications of communal sin as described in this chapter?
